text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGE: SRE-oncall (alice) — automated multi-region failover detected anomalies during traffic-shift from eu-north-1 -> us-west-1. Incident ID IR-2026-0315-B. Initial symptoms: elevated 5xx for EU customers and partial route flapping. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/multi-region-failover

alice: I'm on it. @raj @mei join please. Any immediate notes on whether this is a control-plane routing issue or service-level overload?

raj: Network telemetry shows intermittent BGP withdraws from one transit peer in eu-north-1 beginning 07:03 UTC. Our gradual shift controller kept oscillating weights because some edge routers re-advertised old prefixes intermittently.

mei: App layer shows backend pool in eu-north with healthy checks passing but connection queues exploding (haproxy queue_depth > 400). NLB health checks seem green which suggests stuck connections or upstream saturation.

carlos: Customer impact snapshot: Orders API and Checkout in EU 2xx -> 5xx spike, about 900 errors/minute. Affected enterprise customers reported timeouts. Flagging high-touch for comms.

alice: Triage plan: 1) Pause automated traffic-shift to prevent back-and-forth. 2) If pause doesn't stabilize, prepare manual full cutover to us-west-1. 3) Coordinate session-store replication and salt-cache warming. Who can run the control commands?

raj: I'll handle execution. Commands I'll use (dry run then force):
```
redwood-traffic-shift --app orders --from eu-north-1 --to us-west-1 --percent 100 --dry-run
redwood-traffic-shift --app orders --from eu-north-1 --to us-west-1 --percent 100 --force
```

mei: DNS check: dig shows mixed A records from edge pools — some still resolving to eu-north ingress. Session-store lag briefly spiked to 8s during flapping, now ~3s. Worth noting TTLs are 60s on edge entries.

deploy-bot: Deploy pipeline: eu-north deploys automatically paused due to healthcheck failures.

monitoring-bot: Alert: orders.euw.5xx_rate exceeded warning threshold.

alice: Pause automation now and observe for 90s. Raj run the pause command and report. Carlos hold on external blurb until we decide to force.

raj: Pausing automated shift.
```
$ redwood-traffic-shift --control pause --app orders --from eu-north-1
Control plane: pause accepted, current target 55% -> holding
```

raj: Pause applied. Monitoring for 90s.

mei: Post-pause stats: error rate dipped from 13% -> 9% over last minute but queue_depth still high and tail latency elevated. Some edge routers still reporting eu-north active due to stale route advertisements.

carlos: Draft customer message: "We're aware of increased errors for EU customers due to a regional networking disruption. We're diverting traffic to an alternate region and will update within 30 minutes." Approve?

alice: Approve. Send to SEs and support.

raj: Pause not sufficient. Recommend forced full shift. Will run dry-run and then force in 45s if no objection.

mei: DB replica state: pg-replica lag minimal, redis replication lag ~3s — acceptable. Proceed but expect some session churn.

alice: You have approval to force. Sophia, you'll take the daytime handoff in ~25m. Carlos, prep comms for external update on completion.

raj: Dry-run output:
```
[INFO] dry-run: new route weights eu-north-1=0%, us-west-1=100%
[INFO] estimated transient errors +2-4% due to cache misses
```

raj: Executing force now.
```
[INFO] action: set route weight us-west-1=100 for orders
[INFO] commit id: fshift-20260315-02
[INFO] pushing to global routers...
[INFO] 2026-03-15T07:12:40Z shift: 30% -> 60% -> 100% (completed)
```

raj: Shift shows 100% to us-west-1. Monitoring: 5xx dropping from 13% -> 1.5% over 3 minutes. Latency back to baseline in us-west.

mei: Post-shift checks: eu-north queues drained, us-west backends healthy, no DB failover events. Session continuity: small number of dropped sessions observed, overall acceptable.

monitoring-bot: Alert resolved: orders.euw.5xx_rate returned below threshold.

carlos: External update sent: "We've rerouted traffic to an alternate region; services are recovering. We'll share a follow-up postmortem with root cause and timeline."

alice: Immediate remediation complete. Next steps: 1) Keep traffic in us-west for 60-90 minutes, 2) RCA: raj owns BGP/transit logs, mei owns host/restart and haproxy analysis, 3) Coordinate controlled failback once eu-north stable. Add artifacts and command logs to runbook.

raj: I'll collect bgp adj logs from transit peers, correlate time windows, and open a ticket with provider.

mei: I'll pull haproxy histograms and node syslogs for the incident window to find root cause of connection pile-up.

sophia: Handoff note for daytime oncall: IR-2026-0315-B — network transit instability in eu-north-1 caused automated traffic-shift to oscillate. Forced shift to us-west-1 completed at 07:12 UTC. Severity downgraded to Sev3; monitoring-only. Keep an eye on any reemergence of 5xx for EU traffic.

alice: Handoff accepted. Please attach any snippets and commands used to the incident page: https://redwood.internal/incidents/IR-2026-0315-B/postmortem. Thanks team. :white_check_mark:
